title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving CCCM services to drought affected communities in Buur Hakaba, Berdale and Qansaxdheere

description.narrative:
ltp class="" style=""gtSomalia is facing another severe drought as an estimated 8.25 million people require humanitarian assistance while more than 1.2M are displaced due to the drought. ltspan style="color: windowtext"gtThe risk of famine (IPC Phase 5) remains credible in agropastoral areas of Burhakaba district of Bay Region. The Protracted drought has claimed the lives and livelihoods of many while Women and children constitute more than 80 per cent of those displaced lacking basic services like water, food, and shelter in IDP sites. Due to the unprecedented sixth consecutive season of below-average- April to June 2023 rains, the impact of the drought and increasing economic pressures are deepening the severity of needs and driving the country to the brink of famine. The most vulnerable and marginalized people are disproportionately affected by the drought, including women, children, and minority clans. ltbrgt ltbrgt lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtCESDO through this project, CESDO will operate in an integrated manner with Nutrition, WASH, Health and Protection (GBV) partners in the targeted locations of Berdale, Buur Hakaba and Qansaxdheere to ensure strengthened, integrated response and inclusion of the most vulnerable populations including minority clans. The project will target 13 IDP sites in Berdale, 6 in Buur Hakaba and 18 sites in Qansax Dheere with the following essential CCCM services establishment /strengthening of the CMCs in the 37 IDP sites targeted, provision of capacity building to the CMCs, carry out monthly service mapping and monitoring, facilitate monthly site-level coordination meetings in the 3 targeted districts, community outreach and awareness campaigns to ensure people displaced by drought who join existing sites or set up new sites can immediately receive lifesaving services, conduct weekly new arrival tracking in these settlements, site improvement CFW activities, conduct safety audits, establish/strengthen CFM systems at the sites-level and provide multipurpose solar torches to at risks HHs/survivors to mitigate protection issues including GBV.ltbrgt Through this project, CESDO will reachnbsp36,954 persons in the three targeted districtsnbspwhile the in-direct beneficiaries are 26,762.nbspnbsp
